svg.title: Separate reproductive mode from generation ploidy
svg.desc: The fictional plant runner/seed comparison distinguishes mitotic propagation from fertilization and reshuffling. A Daphnia model permits parthenogenesis in favourable conditions and sexual production of persistent embryos under other conditions, without claiming all species use identical triggers or egg mechanisms. A selected jellyfish cycle has diploid polyp and medusa stages; mitotic asexual production links them, meiosis makes haploid gametes, fertilization restores diploidy and mitotic development returns to the polyp. Intermediate larvae are omitted explicitly. Sea anemones do not acquire a medusa stage by analogy. Animal changes of reproductive mode differ from plant alternation of haploid and diploid generations. Mutation can alter clones; no universal resource or survival ranking is asserted.

g.text: Separate reproductive mode from generation ploidy
Compare mechanisms and context without assigning every animal the same cycle.
Fictional plant: runners develop by mitotic growth; sexual seeds follow gamete fusion.
Runners usually retain the parent genotype; sexual reproduction reshuffles combinations.
Other conditions can favour sex and
egg formation depend on the species.
The jellyfish sequence is a selected simplified cycle, with larval stages omitted.
A sea anemone has a polyp stage; do not add a medusa stage to its life cycle.
Alternating animal reproductive modes do not establish alternating n and 2n adult generations.
Compare time, resource investment and variation in the stated environment; neither mode always wins.
